items.title: Which folds really match?
items.student: Draw/cut a non-square rectangle4cm by2cm,a square3cm by3cm,an equilateral triangle side4cm,and a scalene triangle with sides3,4,5cm. Predict each number of symmetry lines,then fold/trace to test complete coincidence. Show every line on a labelled drawing. A leaf may be only approximately symmetric;do not assume all natural leaves have exact symmetry.
items.teacher: Numbers2,4,3,0 respectively. Rectangle diagonals fail unless square. Equilateral triangle lines join vertices to opposite midpoints. Scalene triangle has none. Symmetry requires the entire figure to coincide,not merely a line passing through its centre. Confirm learner actually constructs/tests shapes;printed answer is not performed evidence.

items.title: Plane-mirror evidence and its limits
items.student: Use a teacher-approved stable acrylic plane mirror,one upright card marker and a marked tabletop line. With mirror vertical on the line,place marker3cm then5cm in front;use a second marker or teacher-supervised tracing arrangement to locate the apparent image position. Record your actual observations and method limits. On paper draw P3cm from line m and locate Pprime so m is the perpendicular bisector of PPprime. Compare distances,lengths,angles and orientation of a labelled asymmetric paper shape and its reflection.
items.teacher: Ideal plane reflection gives equal perpendicular distances3/3cm and5/5cm,congruent lengths/angles and reversed orientation;points on m fixed. A real image appears behind mirror;we do not put a physical marker through glass. Apparent positioning may be uncertain;distinguish measured observations from exact geometric model. Use no sunlight/laser/beams,glass handling or body measurements. Describe virtual upright same-size image only for the plane-mirror setup;not all vehicle mirrors.

items.title: Construct without axes
items.student: On blank paper draw a vertical line m. Mark A2cm left of m;mark B4cm left of m and3cm above A;mark C1cm left of m and4cm above A. Join ABC. With ruler/set square draw perpendiculars to m and construct A,B,C images at equal perpendicular distances on its right. Keep construction lines and label corresponding vertices. Check reflecting twice returns ABC.
items.teacher: Aimage2cm right at Aheight,Bimage4cm right at Bheight,Cimage1cm right at Cheight. Each joining segment perpendicular to m and bisected by it;orientation reverses,shape/area/lengths preserved. Each vertex is constructed independently;do not use an oblique shortest-distance guess. Double reflection in the same line is identity.

items.title: Reflect across x=0
items.student: On the supplied equal-unit grid plot A(1,1),B(4,1),C(2,3). Construct their images in x=0 using equal perpendicular distances. Record coordinates,join both triangles and justify which coordinate changes. Reflect D(0,-2) and E(-3,2) too.
items.teacher: A(-1,1),B(-4,1),C(-2,3);D(0,-2) fixed,E(3,2). Rule(x,y)→(-x,y);x=0is vertical y-axis. Horizontal joining segments have midpoint on x=0. Reflecting twice restores original.

items.title: Reflect across y=0
items.student: On supplied grid plot P(-3,1),Q(1,1),R(-2,4). Draw images in y=0 and justify distances. Also reflect S(2,0) and T(2,-3). Explain why changing both signs would be a different transformation.
items.teacher: P(-3,-1),Q(1,-1),R(-2,-4);S(2,0) fixed,T(2,3). Rule(x,y)→(x,-y);y=0is horizontal x-axis. Both signs changed is a halfturn about origin,not the requested single reflection.

items.title: Reflect across y=x
items.student: Plot A(1,2),B(4,2),C(2,5) on supplied equal-unit grid. Draw y=x and construct reflected triangle. Check each joining segment is perpendicular to the mirror and its midpoint lies on it. Reflect D(-2,3) and E(-2,-2). Explain why swapping coordinates works.
items.teacher: ImagesA(2,1),B(2,4),C(5,2);D(3,-2),E(-2,-2)fixed. Rule(x,y)→(y,x). Joining segment slopes -1for nonfixed points,mirror slope1;midpoints have equal coordinates. Fixed points have x=y. Equal axis scales are required for the geometric45degree view.

items.title: Recover a mirror line on plain paper
items.student: On blank paper mark A and Aprime6cm apart horizontally. Mark B2cm above A and Bprime2cm above Aprime. Construct the perpendicular bisector of AAprime using a compass/ruler or measured midpoint plus set square. Verify it also bisects BBprime at right angles. Join AB and AprimeBprime. Explain why an arbitrary connecting line is not the mirror.
items.teacher: Unique perpendicular bisector through midpoint3cm from each member,vertical;also perpendicular bisects BBprime. Connecting AAimage itself is perpendicular to the mirror,not mirror. For one distinct matched pair the reflection line is uniquely its perpendicular bisector;a single fixed pair P=Pimage alone leaves infinitely many unrestricted lines throughP. Additional pairs test consistency;they do not need separate mirror lines.

items.title: Recover and test the Cartesian mirror
items.student: Use supplied grid. CaseU:A(1,2)→Aimage(2,1),B(1,4)→Bimage(4,1). CaseV:C(-2,1)→Cimage(2,1),D(-1,3)→Dimage(1,3). CaseW:E(1,2)→Eimage(1,-2),F(3,1)→Fimage(3,-2). Draw the mirror for UandV. Test whether Wfits one reflection in the allowed lines x=0,y=0,y=x;explain using distances/midpoints.
items.teacher: U:y=x;V:x=0. Wdoes not fit one of the allowed reflections:Ematchesy=0butFwouldbe(3,-1),not(3,-2). Emidpoint(1,0),Fmidpoint(3,-0.5)cannot both be on y=0;no silent averaging into a mirror. Construct the line and test every given pair.

items.title: A safe design application
items.student: A fictional school emblem uses triangular half A(1,1),B(3,1),C(2,4) and mirror x=0. Draw a complete bilateral emblem and justify how the construction fixes alignment/size. State one practical benefit of symmetric layout and one limitation of symmetry as a quality test. Use classmates’ reasons respectfully;no personal body images.
items.teacher: Otherhalf(-1,1),(-3,1),(-2,4). Corresponding points equal distance/perpendicular across x=0,so equal shape,size and aligned levels. Symmetric placement may support balanced design,manufacture or checking;does not prove material strength,function or universal beauty. Reasoned benefit is evidence for the response,not lasting attitude.

items.title: Road mirrors:application without an unsafe demonstration
items.student: Read this scenario:an adult driver consults a correctly adjusted mirror before a manoeuvre,but an object may still be in a blind spot. Explain a useful role of reflected information and why the mirror alone cannot guarantee safety. Distinguish the ideal plane mirror studied here from a convex vehicle mirror that can widen field but alter image size. Discuss using fictional diagram descriptions only;do not enter roads,vehicles or driving practice.
items.teacher: Mirrors provide some information about surrounding traffic;limited view/occlusion/adjustment/attention mean other appropriate observations are needed. No claim that a mirror eliminates crashes/blindspots. Exact equal-size plane construction does not describe all curved mirrors. Do not supply unqualified road-law or driving instruction. The activity provides a reasoned application/benefit,not competence to operate a vehicle.

items.title: Audit three reflection claims
items.student: Audit:(1)a non-square rectangle has four lines of symmetry;(2)in y=x,the image of(-2,3)is(-3,2);(3)joining one nonfixed point directly to its image gives the mirror. Give corrected statements with drawings/evidence. Then discuss why one fixed pair alone does not determine a unique unrestricted mirror.
items.teacher: (1)Two only;(2)(3,-2),coordinate swap;(3)mirror is perpendicular bisector of joining segment. A fixed point is on the mirror but infinitely many unrestricted lines pass through it unless further information restricts it. Credit actual labelled sketches and clear reasoning,not memorised rules alone.

items.title: Independent reflection construction sheet
items.student: Use this blank equal-unit grid and separate plain paper. This sheet supplies no construction hints. FinalA:triangle P(-4,1),Q(-1,1),R(-3,4),mirror y=0. FinalB:U(-2,1)→Uimage(1,-2),V(-3,2)→Vimage(2,-3). Preserve construction lines. The final questions specify all required work.
items.teacher: FinalAimages(-4,-1),(-1,-1),(-3,-4);mirrorhorizontal. FinalBmirror y=x,bothjoiningsegmentmidpoints(-0.5,-0.5),slopes-1andlineitselfslope1. Plainpaper final:see assessment key. Keep this card out of teaching pack;do not annotate learner grid with solutions.
